chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Safwan al-Jammal, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr), and he said: 'It is obligatory upon the young and the old, the free and the slave, for every person a sa' of wheat, or a sa' of dates, or a sa' of raisins.'
And from Abu Hamzah, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: 'The owners of camels, cattle, and sheep give in Fitrah one sa' of aqit (dried curds).'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr (alms of breaking the fast)
key_terms.صَاع: Sa' (a traditional unit of volume measurement)

ai.seo_question: What are the items and amounts for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the universality of Zakat al-Fitr, emphasizing its obligation on every individual regardless of age, gender, or social status, thereby reinforcing the concept of communal purification. It further illustrates the jurisprudential flexibility (ikhtiyar) within Shia fiqh by permitting livestock owners to discharge their obligation through the payment of aqit (dried curds), reflecting the practical economic considerations of the time. This ruling underscores the hadith's role in defining the material scope of the obligatory charity as a means of spiritual cleansing before Eid prayers.
